authority.subjectBinding: subjectId MUST reference exactly one authoritative USER identity in D1-01 for the assignment lifetime.

fields.name: id
fields.authorityReason: Each assignment is a distinct auditable authorization fact.

fields.name: subjectId
fields.authorityReason: Authorization assignments are bound to one authoritative user identity.

fields.name: roleId
fields.authorityReason: Role identifiers MUST come from the canonical machine-readable layer vocabulary.

fields.name: scopeType
fields.authorityReason: Assignments may be platform-global or limited to an existing organization/IP scope.

fields.name: scopeId
fields.authorityReason: Global assignments have no scopeId; organization/IP assignments reference an already-authoritative scope.

fields.name: status
fields.authorityReason: Revocation must be durable and must immediately remove the assignment from the eligible set.

fields.name: validFrom
fields.authorityReason: An assignment becomes effective only at or after its authoritative start time.

fields.name: validUntil
fields.authorityReason: Optional expiry provides deterministic temporal validity; end time is exclusive.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.authorityReason: Status/revocation changes require an authoritative update timestamp.

eligibility: subjectId MUST equal the authenticated USER subject being evaluated.
validUntil MUST be null or evaluation time MUST be < validUntil.
For scopeType=organization or ip, scopeId MUST be present and the referenced scope MUST itself be authoritative and currently applicable.
A RoleAssignment does not establish Organization Membership, IP ownership, Resource Ownership, Entitlement, Subscription, Verification, or Account State.
rules.roleMapping: roleId MUST match exactly one role identifier declared by contracts/authz/layers.json; unknown or forbidden roles are invalid.
rules.uniqueness: Concurrent effective duplicates are forbidden for the tuple (subjectId, roleId, scopeType, scopeId). Historical REVOKED or expired assignments may coexist.
rules.roleChange: Changing a role or scope is represented as revoking the prior assignment and creating a new assignment; the prior immutable role/scope facts are not overwritten.
rules.revocation: Transition ACTIVE -> REVOKED removes eligibility immediately; revocation MUST increment role_version or the authoritative equivalent and invalidate authorization cache state under contracts/authz/authz-cache-invariant.json.
rules.authorizationVersion: Any change that alters the effective RoleAssignment set MUST advance the authoritative role_version used by authorization caching.
rules.effectivenessEvidence: An assignment becomes effective only after an authorized administrative/system action is recorded with audit provenance; client-supplied role names, JWT claims, verification state, entitlement, subscription, membership, cache, IP or device signals cannot establish an assignment.

globalLayerResolution.eligibleAssignments: Only ACTIVE, temporally valid assignments with scopeType=global participate in the authLogin/authRefresh response layer.
globalLayerResolution.scopedAssignments: organization- and ip-scoped assignments authorize scoped resources only and MUST NOT change the global authLogin/authRefresh layer.
globalLayerResolution.mapping: Resolve each eligible global roleId directly through contracts/authz/layers.json.
globalLayerResolution.multipleAssignments: When multiple eligible global assignments exist, select the highest numeric L0-L8 layer. Equal-layer assignments are equivalent and require no secondary precedence.
globalLayerResolution.noValidGlobalAssignment: Do not synthesize a layer from any non-RoleAssignment input. If no valid global assignment resolves to L0-L8, authentication/token issuance or refresh MUST fail closed using the existing canonical authentication/error contract; no new error enum is introduced.

rules.accountState: Non-ACTIVE account state is rejected by the existing account-state security gate before successful token issuance/rotation; layer resolution cannot bypass that gate.
rules.representation: The authLogin/authRefresh layer is derived from current authoritative assignments at evaluation time. It is not persisted as User.layer and no duplicate layer entity is introduced.
rules.cache: Layer/role changes, revocations and relevant scope changes participate in authorization-cache invalidation; cache state is never authoritative.

invariants: Role is an authorization input; Layer is a derived capability level and is not itself an authorization source.
Verification, RoleAssignment, Entitlement, Subscription, Organization Membership, Account State and Ownership remain separate authorities.
Client-controlled input cannot create or elevate a RoleAssignment.
Revoked or temporally invalid assignments are never effective.
Organization/IP scope does not become global authorization merely because the subject has that scoped role.
No assignment may grant access beyond the resource ownership/scope checks required by the Canonical Authorization Decision Contract.
nonGoals: No new Worker or D1 domain.
No change to existing authLogin/authRefresh wire DTOs.
No promotion of ENT-ROLE-ASSIGNMENT to VERIFIED without implementation, persistence and runtime evidence.

contractReconciliation: Reconcile this authority contract with docs/301, docs/303, contracts/authz/layers.json, contracts/authz/authorization-decision.json and contracts/authz/authz-cache-invariant.json.
Record the explicit multi-assignment/global-layer rule in the Mapping-0 Change Control.
resolverAdmission: Define the deterministic W01 resolver binding without changing the authority semantics.
Prove global-role selection, scoped-role exclusion from global layer, account-state deny, revocation/version invalidation, and no-assignment fail-closed behavior.
implementationEvidence: D1/persistence evidence when implementation is introduced.
Evidence Registry record bound to the validating commit.
